items.title: Karnataka HC upholds eviction of doctor from home over harassment of his 82-year-old mother
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has upheld the eviction of a government doctor from his residence after his 82-year-old mother alleged that he and his wife were harassing her and interfering with her peaceful life [ Dr. M S Mahesh v. Deputy Commissioner ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj took note of Section 22 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. Among other provisions, this Section calls on the State to to frame an action plan for the protection of life and property of senior citizens. The High Court held that the expression "protection of life and property of senior citizens” under Section 22 is wide enough to protect a senior citizen's enjoyment of her home. The Bench added that the statutory protection extends beyond the mere payment of maintenance and can include removing any source of harassment from a senior citizen's residence where the facts justify such action. “For a senior citizen, it carries with it the right to live with dignity, and that includes the right to reside peacefully in her own home without fear, harassment or humiliation,” the Court said in its August 6 order.
